summary: Opaque 429s observed during priority-weighted cold-starts for high-concurrency tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Nimbus Health reports intermittent 429 responses (~0.8-1.2% of requests) for a single enterprise tenant during morning traffic warmups. Throttles present only during short, high-concurrency bursts immediately after their scheduled autoscaler cold-start window (07:45-08:05 PST).

Impact:
- Customer reports degraded UX for real-time patient triage flows (high priority SLA).
- Errors are transient but correlate with scheduled warmup/autoscaler events and a heavy mix of low-latency chat calls + background batch embed requests.

Environment:
- Tenant: Nimbus Health (enterprise account)
- Deployment: Dedicated pool pinned to us-west-2, priority-weighted routing enabled (weights: real-time=0.7, batch=0.3)
- Models: redwood-llama-70b-v1 (primary), rw-open-pt-20b-q4 (fallback)

Observed behavior:
- 429s appear only during the first 2-3 minutes after cold-start cycles and again during small autoscaler scale-ups.
- 429s carry throttle headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: ~22s, but token accounting dashboard shows tenant token balance not fully depleted.
- Console traces show surge of queued requests at the gateway and a short-lived spike of 5xx->429 conversions in the rate-limiter.

Expected behavior:
- Priority-weighted routing should preserve a reserve for low-latency routes during warmup and surface informative retry headers to the client.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Schedule load: 150 concurrent short chat sessions + 40 parallel batch embedding jobs that start within the same 60s window.
2) Ensure Dedicated pool has a cold-start (scale from 0 GPUs) at the start of the window.
3) Observe errors in the first 180s.

Logs/metrics attached below and in linked dashboard references.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a dedicated pool with autoscaler min=0 and scheduled warmup at 07:45 PST
Configure tenant to send 150 concurrent chat requests and kick off 40 parallel embedding uploads within 60s
Enable priority-weighted routing with real-time weight 0.7 and batch weight 0.3
Start traffic and observe rate-limit headers and console traces for 3 minutes
logs_and_metrics: Gateway request logs: spike at 07:45:12 -> 07:46:00 with 80% of connections initiated by single IP range (customer orchestrator)
Rate-limiter metrics: instantaneous token-drain metric shows 90% consumption in 15s but refill reports delayed by ~12s relative to global refill tick
Serving runtime logs: first GPU warmup reported kernel load/start at 07:45:28, KV-cache priming at 07:45:40
Console traces: several requests converted 503->429 in rate-limiter fallback path between 07:45:35-07:45:58
investigation_notes: 03/10 10:15 (Lena): Reproduced in staging by simulating customer traffic pattern; saw 429s within first 90s of cold start when mixer prioritized batch workers concurrently.

03/10 15:43 (Samir Kapoor): Hypothesis A - refill tick misalignment between api-gateway token accounting and rate-limiter leads to short-lived negative token state reported to gateway; investigating clock/tick drift impact.

03/10 17:02 (Diego Morales): Hypothesis B - priority-weighted routing reserve calculation uses steady-state capacity estimates and does not account for initial GPU warmup delays, so reserved capacity not effectively protected during cold start.
03/10 19:30 (Lena): Added an experiment: introduce a small fixed reserve (5% tokens) for real-time route during cold-start window in staging; observed 429s drop to <0.1% in initial tests.
03/11 08:22 (SRE): Gathered relevant traces and CPU/GPU warmup timelines; linked PR that adjusted refill alignment in rate-limiter (github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4321) as potential fix.
03/11 09:10 (Lena): Noted that client SDKs currently may respond with immediate retries that amplify the burst; recommended exponential jittered backoff to customer as mitigation.
Related past tickets: SUP-762318 observed similar warmup 429s post-scale-down, useful runbook patterns identified there.
customer_communication: 03/10 11:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Logged initial ticket with customer, confirmed examples and provided requested request-ids.
03/10 12:30 - Nimbus Health (Customer): Provided their orchestrator logs and confirmed scheduled warmup times. Asked for temporary mitigation until fix is live.
03/11 09:20 - Lena Fischer (Support): Recommended temporary mitigation: stagger batch jobs by 90s or reduce initial batch concurrency, and enable SDK jittered backoff. Customer agreed to test.
03/11 10:05 - Nimbus Health: Implemented staggered start; reported visible reduction in 429s during next warmup window.
temporary_workarounds: Stagger batch embedding job starts to avoid co-located burst with chat starts (>=90s separation)
Apply client-side exponential backoff with jitter for immediate retries during warmup windows
Set pool autoscaler min=1 during high-schedule periods to avoid cold-start entirely
next_steps: Engineering to validate PR#4321 refill alignment change in canary and measure token drift under mixed-priority bursts
Add a short-term server-side reserve policy for real-time routes during detected cold-starts (feature flag rollout for affected tenants)
Update runbook and our priority-weighting docs in Confluence with guidance for scheduled warmups and tenant configuration
Coordinate a follow-up with Nimbus Health to test canary and schedule a low-risk maintenance window if needed
comments: 03/10 11:12 - Aisha Patel: Added initial request-ids and sample payloads from Nimbus for 07:45 incident window.
03/10 16:00 - Samir Kapoor (Applied ML): Observed that model load and kv-cache priming lags the GPU kernel availability by ~10-15s; this likely widens the effective cold period.
03/10 18:45 - Diego Morales (SRE): Spun up a staging experiment to force token-refill alignment change; results show reduced negative-balance windows but need more iterations.
03/11 09:25 - Lena Fischer: Customer performed staggered start mitigation and reports >90% reduction in 429s for subsequent warmup. Scheduling canary test for refill alignment change today.
03/11 12:40 - SRE: Canary for PR#4321 running in us-west-2 canary pool; monitoring dashboard linked.
resolution_notes: In progress - engineering canary rolling. Short-term mitigation recommended and tested (staggering + client backoff + raising min replicas). If canary confirms, plan server-side reserve feature flag for priority-weighted routing during warmups.
If resolved, will include postmortem with timeline and a doc update describing recommended tenant autoscaler settings for scheduled warmups.
